proposed_edit.new_declaration:
theorem Submodule.starProjection_le_starProjection_iff {U V : Submodule 𝕜 E}
    [U.HasOrthogonalProjection] [V.HasOrthogonalProjection] :
    U.starProjection ≤ V.starProjection ↔ U ≤ V := by
  simp_rw [← coe_le_coe_iff, (isSymmetricProjection_starProjection U).le_iff_range_le_range
      (isSymmetricProjection_starProjection V),
    coe_starProjection_eq_isComplProjection, IsCompl.projection_range]

candidates.requested_change: Rewrite the `simp_rw` line to use `(isSymmetricProjection_starProjection U).le_iff_range_le_range (isSymmetricProjection_starProjection V)` instead of the `|>`/`<|` mix, keeping the rest of the simp set unchanged.

candidates.claim: In `LinearMap.IsSymmetricProjection.le_iff_range_le_range`, the final `simpa ... using U.mem_iff_norm_starProjection _ |>.mpr <| ...` again mixes `|>` and `<|`. This is less idiomatic than directly applying `(.2 ...)` / `(.mpr ...)` to the term, and can be rewritten without changing structure.

proposed_edit.new_declaration:
theorem IsSymmetricProjection.le_iff_range_le_range {p q : E →ₗ[𝕜] E}
    (hp : p.IsSymmetricProjection) (hq : q.IsSymmetricProjection) : p ≤ q ↔ range p ≤ range q := by
  refine ⟨fun ⟨_, h2⟩ a ha ↦ ?_, fun hpq ↦ (hp.sub_of_range_le_range hq hpq).isPositive⟩
  specialize h2 a
  have hh {T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetricProjection) : RCLike.re ⟪T a, a⟫_𝕜 = ‖T a‖ ^ 2 := by
    conv_lhs => rw [← hT.isIdempotentElem]
    rw [Module.End.mul_apply, hT.isSymmetric]
    exact inner_self_eq_norm_sq _
  simp_rw [sub_apply, inner_sub_left, map_sub, hh hq, hh hp,
    hp.isIdempotentElem.mem_range_iff.mp ha, sub_nonneg, sq_le_sq, abs_norm] at h2
  obtain ⟨U, _, rfl⟩ := isSymmetricProjection_iff_eq_coe_starProjection.mp hq
  simpa [Submodule.coe_starProjection_eq_isComplProjection] using
    (U.mem_iff_norm_starProjection _).2 (le_antisymm (U.norm_starProjection_apply_le a) h2)

candidates.requested_change: Rewrite the last two lines to avoid the `|>.mpr <|` style, e.g. `simpa [...] using (U.mem_iff_norm_starProjection _).2 (le_antisymm ... ...)`.
